title: Victory for Hemp Shows Prohibitionist Have Problems With Mandatory Stupidity. The Prohibitionist Dilemma Is That They Are Addicted to Bad Arguments.

content_html_sanitized:
Posted February 11, 2004
Analysis by Richard Cowan

I have not written about hemp in almost a year. In fact, the last time I had occasion to do so was during the 2003 NORML conference.
See
NORML Conference Cheers News That Federal Appeals Court Blocks DEA Attempt to Ban Hemp Foods. Industry Optimistic That Courts Will Recognize Absurdity of Rule.

As I reported then, the DEA has lost yet another battle in its efforts to ban hemp foods because there may be trace amounts of THC in them. A three judge panel on the 9th Circuit (the Western states) of the US Court of Appeals was unanimous, and one of the judges was a conservative Reagan appointee.
For an explanation of the ruling see
FEDERAL COURT REJECTS DEA BAN ON HEMP FOODS

While the Feds can appeal the ruling to the Supreme Court, they may decide to cut their losses on the hemp foods issue, because this is their weakest argument legally and logically, and they are very unlikely to win, even in this conservative Court.

I have always been optimistic about our winning this, but it has been a long and expensive struggle against the infinite resources of the federal government. Common sense should not so costly, but then, common decency seems to have been priced out of the market.
See
Ninth Circuit Upholds Patients Right to Use Medical Cannabis. Feds Certain To Appeal to Supreme Court.
and
If Cannabis Could Cure Cancer, They Would Tell Us, Right? No. Very Simply, It Would Undermine Cannabis Prohibition. Steve Kubby Is The Living Proof.

Typically, MPP immediately sent out a fundraising email implying that they were responsible for this win.
See
Richard Cowan Resigns from Board of NORML Foundation. The People It Helps Should Not Be Held Hostage To Rob Kampia's Fear Of the Truth On MarijuanaNews.com

However, the real heroes behind this victory are the Hemp Industry Association and Votehemp.org with special thanks to David Bronner of Dr. Bronner's Magic Soaps and Dr. Bronner's Magic Alpsnack.

Whether or not the DEA appeals this ruling to the Supreme Court, there is still the danger that a prohibitionist in Congress may act by putting a rider (unrelated amendment) on some important bill and change the law to give the DEA the power that it is trying to get the old fashioned way by usurpation.

Mark Souder, the prohibitionist fanatic from Indiana, would be the most likely prospect to do their dirty work. (Souder is responsible for the smoke a joint and lose your student loan bill.)
See
Drug Arrest Record Disclosures On Student Loans Go Into Effect
and
Learning About Prohibitionism: House Debate on Medical Marijuana Bill Offers New Insight Into Police State Ideology.
and links.

An appeal to the Supreme Court or even threatened legislation in Congress would inhibit new investment in hemp food products, but it would also cost the prohibitionists politically. An attempt to change in the law would generate more bad publicity and incur the wrath of the powerful health food industry.

Nonetheless, because the reefer madness set is the hardcore constituency of the drug war generally, the DEA may feel compelled to fight until the bitter end no matter what the costs.
See
UN Agency Tries to Get Swazis To Switch From Insangu To Hemp Cultivation. Weird, And Sad, But Interesting.

They have the same problem with medical cannabis. Logically, they would be better off cutting their loses on an issue where they have at least 75% of public opinion against them, but they cannot.
See
Democracy, Cannabis and the Drug Czar. Arrests Remain Close to Record Levels. Support for Medical Cannabis Now Up to 80%. And 34% Favor Full Legalization. We Are Winning, But The People Are Suffering.

The long term importance of hemp is well understood, but even many hemp supporters may not realize that it is a matter of life and death importance to some people. I know patients who depend on hempseed foods and hempseed oil to cope with diseases ranging from sickle cell anemia to diabetes. While it is at least possible for patients to get contraband marijuana on the streets it would be virtually impossible for a patient to get hempseed oil on the black market.

Consequently, while there is no way to know how many are dependent on the therapeutic qualities of hemp foods, for these people the suppression of these products by Congress could be fatal.

Although the Congress is now busy posturing around Janet Jackson's Half-Time Half-Monty, they can always find time to posture around fighting drugs in an election year. But they might realize that this would make them look even more ridiculous. Clearly, the prohibitionists don't mind killing innocent people, but we may be able to convince them that looking dumb in an election year is not helping W. and it won't help them either.
